subject: Re: Reranker integration & eval questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the call — next steps (reranker integration + eval)

Hi Jenna,

Thanks again for taking time today — good discovery conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up the technical follow-up: 

Recap (what I heard):
- Use case: internal clinical guidelines + knowledge base search + rerank to surface the most relevant snippets for clinicians.
- Corpus size: ~2M documents (mix PDFs, notes, guidelines).
- Traffic baseline: expected steady-state ~3-5 QPS with peak bursts to ~20 QPS.
- SLOs: UI requires top-5 results under ~200ms ideally; backend can tolerate longer for full candidate generation.
- Constraints: Data residency / PHI concerns — you'll be evaluating private deployment options or strict VPC networking.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) I attached a short eval plan and a sample query set (acme_sample_queries.csv). Please confirm: is that representative?
2) Can you share a small labeled eval set (200-500 queries) or let us know labeling format (binary relevant / graded relevance)?
3) We'll propose a two-stage architecture: embeddings-based retrieval to pull a candidate pool, then a cross-encoder reranker to improve final ordering. See the suggested knobs below.

Suggested initial config (we'll tune after an offline eval):
- Retriever: embeddings + ANN index, candidate_pool_size=100
- Reranker: cross-encoder or generative reranker, rerank_top_k=5 (for UI)
- Tune knobs: retriever top_k (100), reranker_top_k (5), diversity/recall threshold for fallback

I'll follow up with a short technical note showing SDK/auth examples, ranking API params, and recommended metrics for evaluation (MRR, nDCG@5/10, Recall@50). Marcus is CC'd and can run the first pass evaluation once we have the labeled set.

Proposed timeline:
- You confirm sample queries + send label set by Wed (2026-10-07)
- We run initial offline eval and share results in ~5 business days

Thanks — happy to hop on a technical session with your engineering team if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: reranker_eval_plan_v1.pdf (high-level eval plan + metrics)
Attachment: acme_sample_queries.csv (50 sample queries)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — next steps (reranker integration + eval)

Hi Jenna — great, thanks for confirming. Answers and details below.

1) Label format (recommended)
- CSV columns: query_id, query_text, doc_id, relevance (0 = not relevant, 1 = relevant, 2 = highly relevant).
- If you can include a short rationale field that helps (optional).

2) Retriever choices (sparse vs dense)
- For clinical text with many synonyms/abbrev: a hybrid approach often works best. Start with dense embeddings (semantic match) + BM25 sparse signals as a feature in candidate scoring. Dense retrieval handles synonyms well; BM25 helps with exact matches and rare terms.

3) Reranker / Ranking API examples (high-level)
- Typical flow:
  a) Embed query -> ANN search -> retrieve N candidates (candidate_pool_size, e.g., 100)
  b) Send candidates + query to reranker -> get final scores and top-K results (rerank_top_k, e.g., 5)

- Example request (pseudocode text):
  POST /v1/ranking/rerank
  body: {"model":"rw-reranker-1", "query":"<text>", "candidates":["doc123","doc456", ...], "params": {"candidate_pool_size":100, "rerank_top_k":5, "return_scores":true}}

- SDK: see https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk-quickstart for python/js examples. We'll also send a short notebook showing embedding -> ANN -> rerank pipeline.

4) Starting knobs we recommend to tune: 
- candidate_pool_size: 100 (start) -> tune 50-500 depending on throughput
- rerank_top_k: 5 (UI)
- latency/throughput: try a cross-encoder for best relevance (higher latency), or a lightweight generative reranker for sub-200ms budgets.

5) Evaluation metrics (we typically report):
- MRR@10 (Mean Reciprocal Rank)
- nDCG@5 and nDCG@10
- Recall@50 and Recall@100 (to evaluate retriever coverage)
- Precision@5 and MAP if you have graded relevance

6) Privacy / deployment note
- For PHI you can run Redwood Private (VPC) or provision a dedicated cluster in your cloud account. We can provide a checklist for SOC2 / PHI safeguards if needed.

Attachments: I attached a short eval plan (reranker_eval_plan_v1.pdf) and a sample script.

Next steps I propose:
- Jenna: share the labeled CSV (500 queries) by 2026-10-07 if possible.
- Marcus / Neha: run initial offline eval on 500 queries -> report MRR/nDCG/Recall in ~5 business days.

If helpful I can schedule a technical deep-dive — let me know.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the call — next steps (reranker integration + eval)

Thanks — looping in a couple quick technical clarifications so we run the eval properly: 

1) Label granularity: If Acme gives graded labels (0/1/2) we'll map to gains for nDCG. Please confirm whether the doc_id values in the CSV match the IDs in their export.

2) Candidate pool generation: we'll test two retrieval configs in parallel:
   - Dense-only (embeddings w/ HNSW) candidate_pool=100
   - Hybrid (BM25 + dense features) candidate_pool=100

3) Reranker models to test: rw-crossencoder-1 (higher accuracy, higher latency) and rw-genrerank-1 (lower latency, generative re-ranker). We'll report nDCG@5, MRR@10, and Recall@50 for each combo.

4) Tuning targets: what's an acceptable baseline for Acme? Jenna, if you have product targets, share them — otherwise we'll aim to beat your current baseline by at least +0.10 nDCG@5 or reach nDCG@5 >= 0.60 as an initial objective.

5) Eval infra: ideally we get a 500-query labeled sample and a mapping to doc_ids. If PHI prevents sending doc text, we can run the eval on your side with our eval script — you'll just need the notebook.

I'll spin up a job once we have the labeled CSV and a brief mapping file. ETA: 3-5 business days for the first run.

--Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
